title: Aperture surface and tool contract playbook (PRD draft)
body:
Purpose and rough scope:

- Problem statement: developers building rich client integrations need a single, low-latency surface for mixed responsibilities: streaming text, incremental structured payloads, and light-weight tool invocations. Current SDK patterns feel heavy: lots of framing, unclear retry semantics, and poor telemetry that makes diagnosing partial failures hard.

- Goal: define a compact, opinionated client surface ("Aperture") that makes tool calls first-class, preserves streaming partials, and gives clear upgrade paths for structured outputs without bloating mobile/client footprints. Deliverables for this PRD: API sketches, ergonomic flow examples, open questions, acceptance criteria, rollout plan.

Design principles (high level):
- Minimal cognitive surface: prefer a single client object with explicit call modes rather than several ad-hoc endpoints.
- Deterministic failure semantics: clearly defined idempotency + at-least-once vs exactly-once semantics for tool calls.
- Observable partials: every partial/chunk must be addressable by sequence id and optional semantic tag so we can measure token-level latencies and parse failures.
- Tiny runtime: keep the client binary <250KB delta for mobile; no large parsing libs required to get useful structured output.

Aperture surface sketch (proto):
- Client: ApertureClient(config)
- Methods:
  - generateStreaming(request) -> Returned: stream events (text_chunk | structured_frame | tool_invocation | meta)
  - invokeTool(toolId, args) -> returns tool ack plus optional streamed outputs
  - resume(sessionId, resumeToken) -> resumes a broken stream, replays tool decisions if necessary

Event envelope (human readable sketch):
- { "seq": 1, "type": "text_chunk", "text": "...", "ts": "..." }
- { "seq": 2, "type": "structured_frame", "schema": "contact_v1", "payload": "{...}" }
- { "seq": 3, "type": "tool_invocation", "tool": "search.docs", "args": "{q:\"...\"}", "invocation_id": "inv-12" }
- { "seq": 4, "type": "tool_result", "invocation_id": "inv-12", "status": "ok", "payload": "{...}" }

Key ergonomics notes:
- Tool invocations should be initiated by the model (server-side) but surfaced to the client as explicit events. Client SDK handles local simulation / optimistic UI by allowing optional pre-registered tool adapters.
- Provide a tiny adapter interface: registerToolAdapter(toolId, invokeFn) — adapter only needs to implement call, cancel, and serialize result. Keep adapter contract intentionally small so mobile engineers can shim easily.
- Default behavior: tool_invocation event -> accepted by server, client receives invocation_id -> client displays 'tool in progress' UI. If a local adapter is present, the client SHOULD call it and send back a locally-simulated tool_result to the server via a resume/patch endpoint (opt-in).

Structured output handling:
- Serve both typed frames and lenient JSON fragments. New clients should prefer schema-first frames (schema id included). Old clients can receive a text_chunk + schema hint for migration.
- Introduce a short, stable schema registry id (e.g., contact_v1) embedded on frames. Validators (on console) will be able to attach examples and regression checks.

Streaming semantics and resumption:
- Streams are sequence-numbered and checkpointed periodically by the server. Checkpoint metadata includes latest seq, a short resume token, and the set of open invocation_ids.
- Resume semantics: client calls resume(sessionId, resumeToken). Server replays missing events and indicates if any tool invocations were observed in the interim (conflict resolution policy described below).

Tool call conflict and idempotency model (proposal):
- Invocation ids are canonical: server assigns an invocation_id at first observed tool intent. Client local simulation MUST use a temporary local id and then reconcile with canonical invocation_id on resume.
- Retry policy: server publishes invocation state (pending, in_progress, completed, failed). Clients may re-send local results only if their local adapter reported the same invocation signature and they have not received a canonical tool_result for that invocation_id.
- Conflict resolution example: if two clients simulated the same invocation_id with different results, server chooses canonical result by trust policy (e.g., server-side execution wins, or customer-configured policy). Client receives a conflict event and should surface a reconciliation UI.

Observability requirements:
- Token-level latency histograms (client send -> first text_chunk, client send -> first structured_frame, tool invocation round-trip).
- Event-level error tagging: parse_error, schema_mismatch, tool_timeout, resume_conflict. Tags emitted by clients are indexed by route/model/tenant.
- Per-invocation tracing: attach short trace ids to tool_invocation events for correlating with backend traces (span id as string).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- SDKs (JS + Kotlin) implement ApertureClient with generateStreaming and resume surface.
- Server emits sequence-numbered envelopes and resume tokens for 99% of requests.
- Tool invocation envelope is accepted and round-trip completes within SLA for >95% of simple tools (echo/ping).
- Basic observability dashboards: token latency, resume success rate, common schema_mismatch examples.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experiment, internal): ship JS prototype + internal demo app, collect developer feedback.
- Phase 1 (beta): expose Aperture surface to a subset of customers as an opt-in flag; collect metrics and first production workloads.
- Phase 2 (general availability): default to Aperture surface for new streaming sessions, provide migration docs and console tooling for schema registry.

Open questions / risks:
- Resume complexity: server-side checkpointing adds state; how much memory/time cost per session are we willing to accept? (SRE input required).
- Security: when clients locally simulate tool calls and patch results back, how do we ensure we don't introduce data exfiltration risks? Need to formalize allowed adapter capabilities and telemetry filtering.
- Mobile offline behavior: do we permit full offline tool simulation then bulk sync? Likely out of MVP scope.
- SDK ergonomics conflict: some customers prefer explicit two-phase tool calls (declare intent -> call). Aperture blurs line by making tool_invocation a first-class event. We should allow an explicit mode flag for strict two-phase flows.

Next actions (short):
- Action: engineering to provide rough cost estimate for server checkpoint storage and resume replay complexity (owner: Tom). Due: 11/20/2024.
- Action: DX to prototype JS client demo and a tiny web UI showing sequence replay (owner: Maya). Due: 11/29/2024.
- Action: Security to draft allowed-adapter capabilities and review exfiltration scenarios (owner: Samira). Due: 11/25/2024.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Could compress envelopes for mobile with a micro-binary framing (length-prefixed msgpack) but keep text-first fallback for web devs.
- Consider a "soft schema" mode that accepts fuzzy matches and emits guided fixes in the console.
- Might pair with Optimize to recommend quantization on large schema payload pipelines.

References and links:
- Slack thread: #hosted-api aperture proposal (see SLACK-#hosted-api/thread-456)
- Related GH PR: GH-PR-7890 (aperture prototype)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1234 (schema registry draft)

End of draft.
summary: Draft PRD for 'Aperture' client surface: compact streaming + structured frames + tool invocation model. Proposes event envelope, resume semantics, adapter contract, observability, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan.
